newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Implied rate shows Italy rates falling.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Implied rate shows Italy rates falling.

text.p: The Italian money market continues to see room for lower interest rates on a one-month horizon, with greater scope for easing further out, a study on implicit overnight rates by the Bocconi University research arm Igier showed on Thursday.

On a one-month horizon the implicit overnight rate is seen at 7.78 percent, fractionally up from 7.71 percent forecast a week ago but down from the actual market rate of 8.00 percent on Wednesday, the day on which Igier based its study.
On a three month horizon, the implicit overnight rate is 7.44 percent from 7.45 percent seen a week ago and 7.96 percent seen a month ago.
The Bank of Italy unexpectedly cut its key discount rate to 7.50 percent from 8.25 percent on October 23 and lowered the fixed term advances or Lombard rate to 9.00 from 9.75 percent.

On a one- and two-year timeframe, expectations for interest rates do not vary greatly from a week ago with the implicit rate for one year hence 6.90 percent compared with 6.99 and the implicit rate on a two-year timespan seen at 7.33 from 7.29 percent last week.

The spread between the Italian implicit overnight rate and the German implicit overnight rate two years hence, which is seen as a good indicator of market confidence in European monetary union, is 236 basis points, virtually unchanged from last week but lower than 266 a month ago.
